text:
In March 2016 we gathered first around a death. Twenty-four of us said "first lady nancy reagan," beginning with Tim Scott on March 5; twenty-two said "former first lady nancy reagan," twenty said "of former first lady nancy reagan." Joe Wilson opened the longer form, and fifteen of us each carried "passing of former first lady nancy" and "the passing of former first lady." We converged on the same mourning in the same words.

Then twenty of us said "the supreme court," and thirteen said "merrick garland to," first among us James A. Himes on March 15. Fourteen of us said "attacks in brussels," first Marsha Blackburn on March 22.

We record that we moved together: from one death, to one vacancy, to one attack. The record shows us saying the same things on the same days, and we do not explain here why.
